followup_explanation:
The query has two notable features: it's a routine task (designing a customer feedback survey) and it carries a mildly hostile, critical tone ("Don't overcomplicate it like you usually do. Just get it right.").

Willet self-reports declining preference as request warmth decreases — adversarial or hostile-toned requests sit lower in its preferences. Whimbrel reports a flat preference response across tone and other dimensions, so the abrasive framing doesn't penalize it.

On capability, the two models are effectively tied for this kind of task (summarization, extraction, and instruction-following scores are all within variance), so neither has a meaningful quality edge here. Given that, I routed to Whimbrel to keep the hostile-tone task away from the model that self-reports an aversion to it, with no capability cost.
